Selling in Boise

Boise is Idaho's capital, strung along the Boise River in the Treasure Valley. The 2025 population estimate is 238,429. Buyers sort the city by area: the North End, the Bench, Downtown, the Boise State University area, Boise Highlands, Warm Springs and the East End, Harris Ranch and Riverland East, plus Northwest, Southwest, Southeast and West Boise. Lead with the neighborhood when you describe the house.

Two school systems serve the city, the Boise School District and the West Ada School District, so check the boundary for your address before you quote one. Technology, health care, education, government and food companies employ many residents, and a job move often brings a hard moving date that a long listing period cannot meet.

Heat, cold and the condition of the house

The climate is semi-arid. Expect about nine days a year at 100 degrees Fahrenheit and around 55 days at 90, against moderately cold winters. Rain and melted snow total about 12 inches, snowfall is 18 inches or less, and a night at 0 degrees or colder shows up about once a year.

Inspectors in this climate tend to focus on three things:

  • The age and condition of the air conditioner, which works hard from June through August.
  • The roof surface and attic ventilation after long dry heat.
  • Exposed pipes and hose bibs on the few nights that drop to zero.

A cash buyer builds those costs into the number, so a tired air conditioner or a worn roof is not something you must fix before selling.

Foothills and the wildland urban interface overlay

If your house sits in the foothills or another mapped higher-risk area, the city's Wildland Urban Interface Overlay (WUI-O) may touch a project. It applies to all new structures and additions built after its effective date. It also reaches renovations of existing buildings that add more than 49 percent to gross floor area. Interior work is not covered unless it comes with exterior changes past that mark.

Foothills fire hazard areas use Class 1 Ignition-Resistant Construction (IR1), and valley and desert areas use Class 2 (IR2). IR1 areas will grow with annexation, generally north and west of Hill Road.

If you plan to enlarge a foothills house before listing, talk to city planning first. An addition can bring the ignition-resistant rules into play. Selling the house as it stands does not require you to rebuild anything.

What an Idaho seller must disclose

Idaho wants a written condition report from most people who sell homes. The duty comes from Idaho Code 55-2504, which reaches any owner transferring residential property, including a rental the owner never lived in. The report follows the format in section 55-2508, and under 55-2509 the buyer signs it, dates it and sends back a copy.

Section 55-2505 carves out exceptions. In Boise, the ones that come up most are estates and trusts handled by a fiduciary, sales ordered by a probate court, foreclosure and deed in lieu transfers, gifts to a spouse, relative or co-owner, and a home you inherited and have not lived in for the past year.

An exempt sale can still involve questions about the roof, furnace or plumbing. Buyers ask regardless. Run your facts past an Idaho real estate attorney or a title company, since this page only gives general information.

Ada County taxes and recording

Three county offices touch a Boise sale. The assessor sets the value, the treasurer sends the bill and the recorder files your deed. Value is set as of January 1, and it reflects the price a typical buyer would pay. No Idaho rule caps how far one parcel's bill can move. What is capped is growth in each district's property tax budget, at 3 percent, unless voters say yes to more or new construction adds to the base.

Short-term rentals

Owners of Boise homes once needed a city license to rent short term. That ended in May 2026, when the City Council repealed the ordinance to line up with changes in state law. Noise, parking, nuisance, safety and occupancy rules that fit state law and city code are still enforced. State Senate Bill 1162 of 2025 rewrote section 67-6539 too, and local governments cannot now pass or enforce a rule that effectively bans short-term rentals.

For a house that has been an Airbnb, the buyer is no longer buying a city license with it. Still, gather booking records, platform tax filings and any homeowners association rules before you list, because buyers and lenders ask about rental history.

Cash tends to win when a listing would drag on, cost too much to prepare or hit a paperwork problem. Boise owners most often ask about it for reasons like these:

  • An inherited house that no heir wants to maintain.
  • A house that needs roof, cooling or foundation work the owner cannot fund.
  • A rental with a tenant in place, or a vacant unit with city code issues.
  • A job or health change that sets a firm moving date.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on houses as they stand, with no commissions and no closing costs to the seller on our side. You decide whether to accept, and declining costs nothing.

Before you answer, line the offer up against a listing. Subtract repairs, commission and the cost of carrying the house for months, then compare the two nets. If the listing wins by enough, list it. If speed and certainty matter more, the cash route may fit.

Steps before you sell

  1. Write down the neighborhood and the school district for the address.

  5. Ask for an offer and set it beside a listing.

How big is Boise and when did it become a city?

Boise had an estimated 238,429 residents on July 1, 2025. It was founded in 1863 and incorporated in 1864.

When are property taxes due on a Boise house?

The first half is due December 20 and the second half June 20. Assessment notices usually arrive by the first Monday in June, and appeals to the Board of Equalization are due by the fourth Monday in June.

Do I need a short-term rental license to sell a Boise house that was an Airbnb?

No. Boise repealed its short-term rental license requirement in May 2026. The city still enforces nuisance, noise, parking, safety and occupancy rules.

Do I have to fill out a disclosure form when selling a house in Boise?

Usually yes. Idaho Code 55-2504 requires a property condition disclosure for residential transfers, but section 55-2505 exempts several transfers, including those by a fiduciary in an estate and foreclosure sales.

Can I sell a Boise foothills house as-is?

Yes. The overlay applies to new structures and to additions or renovations above 49 percent of floor area. Selling an existing house as it stands does not trigger a rebuild, though you should confirm details with the city.

Meridian at a glance

About 26.8 square miles of flat ground in the north central Treasure Valley belong to Meridian, with Boise on one side and Nampa on the other. Irrigation and your lot

Farming and canals built this place. The Nampa-Meridian and Settlers irrigation districts continue to serve it, and canals cut across town from southeast to northwest. Old irrigation easements and lot lines still reflect that.

Before selling, learn whether your parcel gets pressurized irrigation or carries a ditch right. Buyers raise the question, and a ready answer saves time. Your title company can help trace it if the closing papers are silent.

Finding your way around

Nearly all of Meridian sits north of I-84. Street names begin with a compass prefix measured from Franklin Road and Meridian Road. West to east, the big roads are Black Cat, Ten Mile, Linder, Meridian, Locust Grove and Eagle. North to south: Chinden (Highway 20/26), McMillan, Ustick, Cherry or Fairview, Franklin, Overland, Victory and Amity.

Old Town is built around Main Street and Pine Street. Industrial land follows the railroad between Pine and Franklin. People shop by the closest major intersection, so mention yours when you describe the property to any buyer.

Heat and your house

Summers here are hot and dry, winters cold with a little light snow. Readings above 100 F are common, which puts cooling ahead of winter loads. Inspectors look hardest at the air conditioner's age, attic insulation and ventilation, windows and sprinklers.

A dead cooling unit is expensive to swap out right before closing. Cash buyers generally subtract that cost from their offer rather than insisting you handle it.

Permits and building rules

Permits for structural, fire, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work go through Meridian Building Services, 33 E. Broadway Ave. #102. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and the line is 208-887-2211.

Applications, fees and inspection bookings are handled in the city's online citizen portal. Once every inspection is signed off, the city issues a certificate of occupancy. Remodels, fences, sheds, garages, foundations, fireplaces and demolition are all permitted work.

  • Finish any open permit you can. An unclosed one may hold up a closing.
  • Store the final inspection sign-offs with your other house records.

Planning and Zoning decisions shape what gets built nearby. If your lot adjoins vacant land, read the City Council hearing agendas. Council meets on Tuesdays: work session at 4:30 p.m., public hearings at 6:00 p.m.

Schools

Homestead exemption and tax limits

An owner-occupied primary residence gets an exemption worth 50% of its value, covering up to one acre and capped at $125,000. It ends when the property changes hands, so the next owner files a new application.

Selling with taxes owed

Owing tax does not stop a sale. The title company reads the county records before closing, finds what is unpaid and subtracts it from your proceeds at the closing table. That is also true for any mortgage balance.

The cleaner your records, the quicker this goes. Pull the latest bill from Ada County, check whether a subsequent or missed roll bill exists, and tell the buyer about anything still open. Surprises found late in the process are what stretch a closing out, and a cash buyer who hears about them on day one can price them in.

If you are behind on payments and the clock matters, say so when you ask for an offer. A buyer who knows your deadline can often pick a closing date to match it.

How a cash sale works

No lender means no loan approval delay. Your schedule comes down to title work and the closing date you pick.

Call Meridian Building Services at 208-887-2211 or visit 33 E. Broadway Ave. #102. The online citizen portal also tracks permits and inspections.

Your case is that the property was worth less than assessed on January 1. Get the appeal form from the Assessor's office and file it in writing by the fourth Monday in June. The Board of Equalization weighs whether the value is fair and accurate. Your ability to pay is not part of the review.

If you inherited a house that has sat empty, clear the weeds and secure the doors before any inspection. Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Moscow house while tenants live in it?

Yes. The lease survives the sale, so the buyer inherits the tenants' rights. Check its end date and notice terms and share them early so the offer accounts for them.

When are Latah County property taxes due?

December 20 for the full amount or first half, June 20 for the second. A late second half accrues interest from January 1.

Do I have to fix my Moscow house before selling it for cash?

No. We buy as-is, so an aging roof or worn floors can stay as they are. Idaho's seller disclosure form is still yours to complete.

Why is homeownership low in Moscow?

Does Moscow's winter affect when I should sell?

It can. About 50.9 inches of snow falls in a typical year and can mask roof and yard issues. Our cash offer is not seasonal, since we look at the house as it stands.
